looks_like_me_why: Overall I see myself — short curly hair, my skin tone, the tortoiseshell glasses and the smile show up well (cover/page 0 and lots of story pages like 1, 3, 4, 9, 12, 18, 20). It's clearly a stylised, childlike version of me though, with bigger eyes and cartoon proportions, so it's not an exact adult likeness. A couple pages felt odd — page 6 shows two Reds standing together which looks like a glitch, and on a few closeups the glasses/hair details shift slightly.
rings_true_why: The text and images follow the classic Little Red Riding Hood beat by beat and the pacing feels right for a children's picture book. The scenes (path, flowers, Grandma's cottage, wolf in bed, woodcutter) all line up with the traditional story and read naturally to a kid.
professional_why: The artwork is high quality and consistent — lovely colors, good lighting, polished characters and backgrounds. It looks like a real published children's book page-by-page; I'd be happy to print or gift this as a physical book.
not_good: Page 6: two Reds standing side-by-side feels like an error. Some small inconsistencies in glasses and hair detail across pages (looks slightly different on a few closeups). A few images exaggerate child proportions so the likeness feels more ‘inspired by’ than true-to-age — not a dealbreaker but worth noting.
liked: I loved that the glasses and curly hair were preserved — that made it feel personal. The cottage and forest scenes (pages 8–10, 18) are cozy and perfect for bedtime reading, and the characters' expressions are great. My kids would adore this!
